olivia_sales: Acme's CI pipeline is failing their POC tests with 401s and 403s intermittently. They hit us during a demo. Can we swarm?
acme_ci: CI job log excerpt: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $RWD_KEY\" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/inference` -> returns 401, then sometimes 403 on different runners.
marc_se: Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) Are you using the hosted endpoint `api.redwood.inference` and Bearer header? 2) Any org/project env vars set in the CI that the SDK might surface?
acme_ci: We use the hosted endpoint and the Go CLI. We set RWD_KEY in GitLab CI variables. No explicit org/project in our job config but we do set RWD_ENV=staging from other projects.
dee_infra: The SDKs attach org/project automatically if env vars named RWD_ORG or RWD_PROJECT exist. But CI runners sometimes source dotfiles or global envs. Can you run a debug job printing env keys prefixed RWD_* (sanitized)?
acme_ci: Pasted sanitized env: `RWD_KEY=rwd-prod_abc123
RWD_PROJECT=legacy-demo
CI_JOB=unit-tests`
marc_se: There's the leak. Your RWD_PROJECT is set to legacy-demo while the key is bound to org-acme/proj-poc. When the SDK sends project header that doesn't match key binding it can return 403, or 401 if the key is disabled/rotated.
acme_ci: Weird — the project var was left over from an internal sandbox. Why would it cause 401 sometimes and 403 other times?
dee_infra: If the key is active and binding mismatches, server returns 403 Forbidden. If the key was rotated/disabled between requests you'll see 401 Invalid API key. With parallel runners some requests hit older cached tokens or different jobs with different envs which explains the flip.
secrets_bot: secrets-service: looked up recent requests for rwd-prod_abc123 -> last_request_id: rwd-req-7f9a2, key status: active, bound_org: org-acme, bound_project: proj-poc, last_rotation: 2026-01-10T12:02:00Z.
acme_ci: We found one runner with an outdated env that had an old key too. Sounds like a mix of env leak + stale key.
marc_se: Two immediate unblock options: (A) remove RWD_PROJECT from CI and restart runners, (B) create a short-lived CI service key scoped to inference-only and bound to the project the CI actually uses. For security questionnaire, you can request embeddings-only or inference-only scopes.
olivia_sales: Customer asks whether we can enforce IP allowlist for CI runners.
dee_infra: Hosted accounts: no per-key IP allowlist for public hosted tier. IP allowlisting and CIDR controls are available for Dedicated/Private customers. For PoCs we can offer short-lived scoped keys as mitigation.
acme_ci: Please create a scoped CI key for our `ci-runner-acme` with 72h expiry and inference-only scope. That will be easiest.
secrets_bot: secrets-service: created key `rwd-test_ci_acme_55`, bound_org: org-acme, bound_project: proj-poc, scopes: [inference:generate], expires: 72h, status: active, id: rwd-test_ci_acme_55.
acme_ci: Deployed new key to CI variables and re-ran job -> all tests green, 200 responses.
marc_se: Follow-ups: 1) Add a quick check in CI to fail if RWD_PROJECT or RWD_ORG env is present but doesn't match expected project; 2) We'll add a console hint to show "bound org/project" next to keys and last rotation time. I'll file both as small UX tickets.
olivia_sales: Also note for the PoC summary: include key id rwd-test_ci_acme_55, expiry, and the security answer about IP allowlist limitations.
dee_infra: Rate-limits note: if your CI parallelism is high, start at 30–50 req/min per runner and use exponential backoff with jitter on 429s. Use batching for embeddings. Monitor `x-rwd-remaining` and `x-rwd-reset` headers.
acme_ci: One last ask from security: can PoC keys be scoped to service accounts only (no human reuse)?
marc_se: Yes — we can generate service-account keys intended for CI with limited scopes and short TTLs. For long-term, Dedicated/Private supports org-managed service accounts with IP controls and KMS.
olivia_sales: Great work. I'll update the PoC runbook with the new key id, CI env checklist, rate guidance, and security notes. Closing swarm. :white_check_mark:
